c.tagline: Germany's car capital, cradled by vineyards and wooded hills.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; Free Now and Uber dispatch the same licensed taxis, so prices are broadly similar and there is little street-hailing outside ranks and stations.

emergency.note: 112 reaches ambulance and fire across the EU; 110 is the direct police line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The Klett-Passage underpass at the main station attracts drinkers late at night, and pickpockets work the Volksfest and Christmas market crowds.

hood_desc: The walkable core around Schlossplatz, the Konigstrasse shopping boulevard, the palaces and the main museums; where first-timers stay to have everything on foot and the Hauptbahnhof on the doorstep.
A leafy, elegant residential quarter of Gruenderzeit apartment blocks, neighborhood cafes and the pretty Feuersee church, a short walk or Stadtbahn hop from the center; calm but well-connected.
A younger, trendier district around Marienplatz and the Heusteigviertel, packed with bars, indie cafes, the Zacke rack railway and a lively going-out scene.
Stuttgart's oldest surviving quarter, a cluster of narrow lanes once home to tanners and winegrowers, now full of galleries, boutiques, workshops and traditional wine taverns (Besenwirtschaften).

A spa and heritage district across the Neckar with Europe's second-richest mineral springs, the Wilhelma zoo and botanical garden, the Mercedes-Benz Museum and the giant Cannstatter Wasen festival grounds.

water.note: Tap water is high quality and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Stadtbahn and S-Bahn run roughly 4:30am-1am; night buses and weekend night trains cover the small hours on Friday and Saturday.
transit.pay: No transit card needed: buy tickets in the VVS mobile app or from station machines (bank cards accepted) and keep them for inspection. A single ride is about 3 EUR (~US$3.30) and a day ticket around 6 EUR; one ticket covers the Stadtbahn, S-Bahn and buses across the zones you buy. Staying weeks? The Deutschland-Ticket (58 EUR/month) covers local transit nationwide.

transit.m: S-Bahn S2 or S3 to Hauptbahnhof (~27 min)

tip.r: 5-10% / round up the bill for good service
